previous_summary: Fail, on one high-severity finding. Outlook-brief.md sections 1 and 4 accuse management of blurring the cause of the General Merchandise decline and of disclosing the space-reallocation programme "only later, in Q&A". Both the transcript's prepared remarks and web-013 in this run's own evidence pack show management named the planned space reduction as the more significant driver up front, and the quoted phrase "seasonal weakness" is cited to claim-002, which is the grocery sales figure and contains no such wording. Three medium outlook findings follow a common thread: the brief is more confident than its evidence in both directions -- a one-sided "clean positive surprise" framing that ignores the GM+Clothing miss and the five-quarter-low headline growth visible in its own cited source, an upside case resting on three uncited direct quotations that never passed the quote gate, and a base-case positioning judgment that the brief's own section 9 disclaims. On the claims side, the extraction captured the beats but not the misses, and isolated the dilution half of a two-sided CFO answer on margin. Deterministic stages all passed and are confirmed present; the injection scan is genuinely clean; sources opened were authentic and correctly dated. Sector language is appropriate throughout -- grocery, general merchandise, loyalty and retail media, with no template metrics borrowed from another industry.
